nameStory: Palmodictyon gets its scientific name from Greek words meaning 'vibrating net,' which perfectly describes how this tiny freshwater algae looks under a microscope - like a shimmering, net-like structure made of interconnected cells. The species name 'varium' means 'variable,' hinting at how this little organism can change its appearance depending on growing conditions.
description: Palmodictyon varium is a microscopic freshwater green algae that forms delicate, net-like colonies in quiet waters. **[UNCERTAIN: Limited knowledge of this specific species - very rare observations suggest caution in description accuracy]** These colonies are typically invisible to the naked eye but can sometimes create faint greenish films or patches in still water. Each colony consists of interconnected cells arranged in a beautiful mesh pattern that can only be properly appreciated under magnification.
